(This review was initial posted to the season 2 finale episode & copy pasted to main page) As someone who doesnt usually gravitate towards shows like this, I was taken by surprise by how much I enjoyed the first season although not saying it was some of the best tv Ive ever seen it pleasantly surprised me.  Turn the page for the second season & what has occurred over the course of 6 episodes to build up to this has been again, nothing revolutionary or "new", but the crisp quality of character development & plot advancement is so close to unmatched to most shows or even movies now a days I think is where it really stands out as an animal of a different kind that we just dont get to see as much as say back when cinemas & the art of what was seen on screen had a higher value than the tasteless pastel colored dribble that monopolies like disney & netflix getting all too comfortable & efficient at pumping out like a lazy fat Al Capone firing a tommy gun from the comfort of his living room/lazy boy while munching on day old popcorn with his free hand saying "now this is what a real gangster looks like". No. No it is not. And the vast majority of said companies are doing that with their "entertainment" and "saying come one come all and be entertained by... well... something, doesnt matter what you like cause whatever it is we got some half thought out show that will scratch that ten second attention span itch till you want something else and we will probably have something new in the works for that too!"  In a way without exactly being able to put my finger on it, I would say White Lotus is ticking off the boxes that made so many of the HBO classics now a days, hits back in the day. It isnt just the drama, or the sex or even the breathtaking scenery.. its the true to reality & its awful tendencies & natures that it gets right with some fantastic acting, crisp screenwriting, and all around great directing. With all those things one would expect greatness but as we have seen with things like The Hobbit or Last Duel, nothing is guaranteed for success or to be "good".  I know those two examples are prob a head scratcher but in my mind the Hobbit had every reason to at least be "good" but I found it intolerable. While Last Duel I wouldnt call an instant "classic" but in my mind without doubt a fantastic movie, yet received almost infuriatingly little attention or recognition despite the absolute insane names on that call sheet. So all to say that I am just happy there are still some shows out there that can strike that cord of old school movies & tv shows while doing in one of the hardest of genres which to me is this intensely mundane realism with a zesty splash of humor, suspense & intrigue. As for what the other details are that make this show so catchy & hard to stop watching I cant quite say but for me, this is a must watch for anyone who isn't a staunch devote religious fanatic. Then again if you are, chances you have ever have had an HBO subscription before is slim to none.

At first, I didn't quite know how to feel about this series. Reading the comments on here I gave it a few episodes and indeed, I started to really like it. Someone wrote that what makes the series great is the writing and the acting and I fully agree. There is nothing especially new or innovative about it, nor are there a lot of booms and bangs - just a series about (rich, privileged and flawed) people, their personal development in the time span of a vacation and the effects these people have on each other. Yet it draws you in and you want to know where they all end up. A pretty solid effort. Now I am off to watch season 2.  Edit: I upgraded my rating after watching season 2. The second season adds profoundness to some of the dialogues. At times, it really does give you something to think about and reflect upon. Clever as well as entertaining. Very well done.

I've followed Mike White for most of his career and he has finally struck gold with The White Lotus - and I, for one, am so happy for him. This is a fantastic show, super entertaining, hilarious, and even has a hint of suspense. Really enjoyed both seasons so far. Excellent cast in Seasons 1 & 2 - especially Jennifer Coolidge. I hope there are many more seasons to come. A+ series with top-notch acting, writing & directing. The locations and cinematography are gorgeous, and it's a terrific juxtaposition when paired with the quirky soundtrack (the music really does grow on you, despite its initial strangeness). Well worth the watch!

The first 2 seasons of the white lotus had such a good flow to them, the pace of each episode was right on point, and the characters were likeable and relatable.  I've watched 2 episodes of this new season and am really not feeling it, it's just off, the storyline boring AF, and unlikeable characters. I was hoping that by the second episode the story and plot would pick up somewhat, but yet nothing. The characters just don't do it for me, and nothing shocking or dramatic has developed so far. This total change of pace for season 3 might work against the show.  I'm about ready to give up on this show if it doesn't pick up.  I will be rewatching the first 2 seasons and skip this mess of a third season.

Oddly entertaining, found myself wondering why I continued watching and then I remembered oh yea... Alexandria Dadarrio.... Damn... you will want to absolutely hate the teenage girls. Some of the most unloveable characters I have ever watched.. weirdly entertaining that's all I can say, and not what I would call a satisfying ending though..

I tried racking my brain for a bit now deciding why this is one of the most important shows, making a contemporary statement in recent memory. At times it feels like the story is using topical culture references as decoration for its allure. On top of this manipulating the Covid brain viewers, with beautiful travel, sceneries, like Sicily, or Hawaii, a low blow. But like good literature, the film takes its characters and storylines, and continues to fold them into each other, and expand beyond the point of a origin. This was inspirational for me, because of the lack of artistic efforts of the past five years (with exception of euphoria, which is more so an adults, exploitation of Gen z culture, then a correct representation of it) in capturing the contemporary life. I really hope that this TV series is looked at as an entry point for further attempts at interpreting the world today, with all its quirkiness, contrived, dialogue, vapid, and binary personalities, as opposed to, an exception. Good art and expression can still go exist with popular interest.
Lots of special moments, lovely scenery and above all the music is the best!

Mike White's approach to a resort populated by the immensely wealthy and powerful is both nuanced, cringey and deep with pathos. While I never truly "feel" for the plights of these characters, the inherent tragedy of their lack of self-awareness makes for an interesting watch. Not to mention the almost existential pain of seeing them go on their merry way, leaving emotional devastation in their wake. Worth watching, if only to make you re-evaluate your life -- and to pretend like you are on vacation.
Supercilious host. Cardboard guests. Sophomoric script would have failed intro screenwriting course. Watched till the boredom overtook us. Enough was by then more than enough.

This is a difficult mini-series to review as it will polarise viewers. Billed as a comedy-drama, there's a little of the latter and almost none of the former. It's cringe-worthy satire with a few giggles now and then.  The eponymous hotel in Hawaii tells the tale of several mainly rich, entitled, white American guests and some staff members with their own issues to explore. Almost all characters are more caricature than realistic but the acting standard is good all round. There are many scenes of dubious relevance which seem like time filler, rather too many doleful shots of waves, and a background score which at times can be overbearing.  It's difficult to like most of the characters. There are themes pertaining to rich entitlement, imperialism, selfishness and anxiety, but they are explored in a somewhat haphazard way. We know from scene 1 that someone dies and by the final episode, I was rather wishing it was most of them. Even that story doesn't quite work.  Overall a good idea but not well executed in my view and do generally unsatisfying.

In all three seasons of White lotus I had similar feelings. I was surprised of how much I liked the weird theme song, I didnt like the characters at first and than they grew on me, and at the end I was thinking - how come this is the first time Im seeing this kind of story. This is genious.  I love that the series keeps the structure that works 1) greeting guests for one week in luxury resort 2) working class people vs. Privilidged wealthy people mixes up with couple of characters who feel bad about being so well off (but just for a little moment) 3) mystery death to be reveiled at the end.  In each season the storylines become a bit more interesting and connecting characters are evolving. Keep that and I will gladly watch another 10 seasons of this. It just works.
Good Drama, well made and good actors. Probably wont watch it again.

Originally I was bowled over by the superb production values and artistic sense of this series. In hindsight, however, and after viewing all episodes of the second season, I have to admit experiencing buyer's remorse. Lovely as it all is, and given license to cast some rather good actors, I have come to dislike both scripts intensely. It is not only that you have far too many loathsome principals, but also that they are made to play cardboard cutouts, turning into improbable and forced events. The end result is nothing more than soap opera. It is not enough to make good guys bad and vice versa, but instead to show believable character development along the way.

When you see "expert critics" pushing you something like the eighth wonder of the world, BEWARE!  Where to start?? This show is simply an artistic fart, no story, no structured characters and plot, BORING AF dialogues, terrible acting I wish I could give this garbage a 0!

I was so excited for season 3 to come out! The cast- Walter Goggins, Parker Posey, Michelle Monaghan so far everyone is outstanding. I was hesitant to get on board with Schwarzenegger but what a standout he is! He is so creepy and cringy in this you totally forget he is technically Hollywood royalty. This young mans performance is noteworthy. You literally forget who he is -he's that good in this.  The writing is what we've come to love and expect with this series, it's dark comedy at its finest. You find yourself thinking "they are not going there and the writers take you straight there ". Love this season.

The White Lotus brings together a variety of characters of wealth to a Haawai hotel in which each character has an impact on one another as they all interwene.  At its core the story is about how oblivious the wealthy are to real everyday struggles and how they find trivial meaningless issues a big problem. It is also about how they need to be seen and feel validated, their self indulged entitlement. Mike White brings many real life issues to the plot including, political view points, sexuality, race, age and gender. The White male privilege is a topical point in contrast to women empowerment and black lives matter. He explores all different views from all walks of life coming together. The interesting aspect is how so many people go on holiday to get away from their problems yet often this can highlight them even more.  The show is top notch in mostly every department from an intense building score to incredible cinematography. The writing is very real with a little playful edge satire amongst an amazing cast. Each actor/actress does a respectable job in understanding their part and differentiating it with individuality.  The standout role for me is (Murray Bartlett) as Armond.

Awesome stuff. Watched it in one sitting, great characterization, decent acting... the scene where Alexandra Daddario crying saying she made a mistake while talking to her husband is the best acting I have seen from her and one of the best I have seen in general. If you enjoy a good drama you should definitely check it out.

The White Lotus is a very unique series. At first when I began to watch it, I was very confused, and didn't think I was going to get past episode three. The story seems to move very slow, and not much is happening. Still, the cinematography, direction, acting, and sound engineering was fantastic so I decided to stick with the show.  As it turns out, The White Lotus isn't moving at a snail pace, but rather it is set up more like a book than your typical TV melodrama...I was just taken aback a bit because the show got very good reviews and I was expecting a break neck pace story with many sub plots to keep the viewer's attention away from their cell phones.  The White Lotus, turned out to be a serious character study with many interesting non-forced conversations about the topics of today. Where the audience is allowed to participate in the conversation rather than to be spoon-fed what we are supposed to believe.  Overall, it was a very pleasant watch and I am referring to season number one, the only one I have seen. Still, my main take away is it is always better to be rich and miserable than to be poor and miserable.  Enjoy!

I find the show very good. What I find suspicious are all the 1 and 2 star reviews. Reading over them I see the same objections made over and over, frequently expressed very similar language. Are these really independent reviews?

Season 1 was a 9/10. Season 2 was tracking to be a 9/10 as well but went to a 7 after Jennifer Coolidge tripped off the boat, hit her legs and died. What a terrible ending.  Season 3 is terrible. I would give it an 4/10. You cannot rewatch season 3 like you can season 1. Our society in America is so pathetic how people will just give out 10/10 or "omg it's amazing". Not watch and go right to "omg this is the best show since sliced bread".

Where better to do it than in a hotel or a resort! So, this is not your immediately simply funny type of show but it asks to use your wits as uncovering today's America's classes is being done in a very smart way. You've got your guests that pretend to be not just guests but rather kin on visit and you got your staff who are acting as this wasn't a hotel but a seaside family reunion. And step by step, whole mess is bound.

Felt like a waste of my time. I would have stopped watching halfway through but there is only 6 episodes. It was really tough to watch the whole series. I like the cast but the storylines were predictable and at the end of the series it just seemed pointless. There are so many better shows out right now I wouldn't waste your time watching this show. I definitely wouldn't recommend it to anyone either.

This show has been frustrating me in so many ways. TWL doesn't know what it wants to be. Is it meant to be a satire? If so, it fails on that account because it bounces between so many different themes that it doesn't successfully satire any one of them. Is it meant to be a gripping drama? If so, it fails because we have no centralized character with which to orientate ourselves in order to relate to the drama. Is it meant to be titillating? If so, it fails because I can see more flesh on a carved Christmas turkey than in this show. Social commentary? Nope, the core cast are a bunch of rich white people, which in and of itself does not constitute commentary. Substance abuse? Depression? Mental illness? Homophobia? Generation gap? ALL of them are alluded to, but none of them have been sufficiently developed to make a show that's even remotely engaging and sensical towards the subjects it seems to want to talk about.  I'm half way through binging the entirety of the run, and I don't care about ANYBODY. The only two characters I don't overly hate are Belinda and Quinn, because they're both so underdeveloped as to be the least abhorrent of the lot. Trying to find a decipherable meaning to any of the events in this show is akin to reading a Faulkner novel. Way too difficult for the amount of energy you have to invest in the process.  I hate this show.

The big names in here are... Jennifer Coolidge, who was so awesome in Best in Show and Two Broke Girls. Molly Shannon, of course from SNL. Steve Zahn, from film and television. At the open, we flash back to The White Lotus, an exotic resort, where something terrible has happened to a honeymoon couple. Everybody... the guests and the employees are all quirky and weird. The running gag seems to be that every time the guests want to do something, they are unable to. For some reason. Either the equipment is broken, or that activity is only available at 6 am. Dad (Zahn) is sure he's dying of cancer. But can't open up to his son, who knows something is on dad's mind. Some fun conflicts with the kids... there's no-where for the teenage son to sleep, and the two girls seem to have a love/hate relationship. And each staff member has their own quicks. But you'll have to watch for yourself. It's fun. There's a sense of adventure and suspense. First season released on hbomax channel. I hope they make more! Written and directed by Mike White, who is SO recognizable from Chuck and Buck! Does a lot of stuff with Jack Black, his business partner.

I suspect that to appreciate this show to the fullest you need to be of a certain age or at least have some life experiences under your belt. But for me (late 40s viewer) it absolutely nailed it. Funny, moving, witty ... just amazing and fun to watch. The cast is stellar, and each scene is interesting to where I could not stop watching. Probably the most fun and tuned into a show since Six Feet Under for me. It is very different, but the comic yet serious adult and social themes create a perfect show. Well done by the cast and entire crew (no I had nothing to do with the production, seriously I'm just an IT guy that works in government).

Great work of art ! Through every seasons the substance and attention that was put in to details, meaning has improved massively. It's only my take on it but I hope that this show will keep on getting renewed. The script is a greater puzzle to solve than I thought it would be. I feel like overall Mike White is enjoying this has much has we do. I liked every season but it's a privilege to see something that was already good get even better. The script, pictures and casting is not something that was chosen randomly and I appreciate the work that was put into it. I'll be waiting for the next season. The only thing I won't do again is listening to this show one episode at the time it's not meant to be. Thank you !
This series reminded me of various vacations I've take at different times in my life. Truly worth watching. The music soundtrack is not helping.

I have to say, I absolutely enjoyed this show.  For a series like this, my overall enjoyment and rating tend to go up when I can binge-watch the episodes instead of waiting week by week. The reason? At the start of each season, the pacing feels incredibly slow. It's almost like the show builds up in slow motion, which can be tough when you're watching it in real-time. But once you hit the second half, everything picks up rapidly, and the drama comes in full force. Watching it all at once really allows you to get immersed in the buildup, whereas waiting week to week makes it harder to stay invested in those slower episodes.  What really stood out for me, though, were the characters. They are brilliantly written-messy, chaotic, and real. Each character feels so nuanced, and the show doesn't rush through their emotional arcs. There's time spent really diving into who they are, their struggles, and their growth, and that's something I deeply appreciate. Shows that take the time to explore their characters' emotional depth are always the ones that stay with me.  Additionally, the location of each season is worth mentioning. It's not just a backdrop but a character in itself. The settings feel incredibly authentic, and the aesthetics are gorgeous to watch on screen. Whether it's the architecture, the lighting, or the atmosphere, everything just complements the tone of the story.  All in all, I'd highly recommend this show, especially if you can watch it in a binge-session. If you're into character-driven stories with rich emotional depth and visually stunning locations, this one should definitely be on your list!

It's a real shame they seem to have decided to take this wonderful programme down the sensationalist route.  With all the shenanigans going on it reminded me of watching a fictional take on Love Island which is such a shame.  It detracts from the brilliant acting skills of some of the cast, especially Jennifer Coolidge who is simply outstanding for the second season in a row.  There are still several standout moments if you cut through Love Island. The actors seemingly have genuine chemistry, the script is mostly strong and the cinematography absolutely outstanding.  I'm sure those of a younger age than me will lap this up, no pun intended (when you watch it you'll get it), and not horrendous for me but could have been so much better if it had been dialled down a couple of notches.

Superb writing, casting and subsequent acting mixed with gorgeous and appropriate island music. Stories of many arguably mostly unlikable and certainly flawed characters wonderfully interwoven to depict the real villain of the story - capitalism and modern western life (especially the rich part of its equation). Very intelligent, but also emotional and very real, whether you are rich, poor or anywhere in-between - just a beautiful social commentary.

This show is about a group of people gone vacationing on an island and also the hotel employees who try to please their guests. The show basically starts with the ending of the vacation where one of the guests waits in the airport while a dead body is being loaded onto the airplane and then the show starts days before.  This type of dark situation comedy isn't my type of thing but the opening did got me hooked to see how they got to that place. There are lots of entertaining awkward cringey gross moments in the show with characters that I didn't really care for. It's not something that I would like to see a season 2 of. I mainly check it out for Alexandra Daddario and Sydney Sweeney.

This show was sooooo boring, nothing much going on and made me feel awkward and uncomfortable. The acting was bad and the characters even worse. Didn't care at all for any of them. I can't believe people are giving it a higher rating then 1. It was abysmal. Just don't get it at all. Strange, weird and boring all rolled into one. Just left confused at how such a bad showed could be made. Just totally in disbelief how bad it was and mad at the time wasted on it. Thought it would get better but only got worse. Avoid at all costs.

Steve Zahn is so versatile and his role as father to two spoiled and fu*ked up children sets the tone for a wild and unexpected vacation in a sunny and expensive resort like most of us could ever imagine. Zahn's wife in the film is played by Connie Britton who rounds out the fearsome foursome. Mossbacher clan. Their daughter Olivia (Sydney Sweeney) is allowed to bring her girlfriend Paula (Brittany O'Grady) just so the two girls can predictably and callously ridicule the masturbating brother Quinn (Fred Hechinger) who gets relegated to sleep in the closet so the girls can have their privacy. Sort of like a male Cinderella with Quinn in the lead role and his sister Olivia and her mean girl girlfriend Paula who both prefer to be doped up while mocking Quinn to no end.  There is also a great supporting cast of both other hotel guests as well as hotel staff and I would be remiss if I did not give special mention to the hotel guest Tanya McQuoid (Jennifer Coolidge) and the gay hotel Manager Armond (Murray Bartlett) who has had just about enough of the uppity and demanding hotel guests.  There are a lot of stories intertwined in this seven (7) episode mini-series and unlike the Love Boat and/or Fantasy Island there is a lot of dirty sex, lots of drugs, and scrupulous guests as well as hotel staff to keep us entertained and wondering what will happen next especially with the fu*ked up Mossbacher family.  I give it an 8 out of 10 IMDb rating with a warning this is strictly for adult entertainment and not for the kiddies.

You idiots that said this was horrible. I would love to know what you think is better?  This is so good it is like a 6 hour film. It rises above the banalities of episodic tv. If you don't think this writing is superior, you have no clue what great writing is. If you can't see the perfection of how every character is arced and there is literally not one scene/line of dialogue that isn't paid off, then you should not be critiquing anything.  Go watch your Marvel films with worn out dialogue and plots so unoriginal that you have seen the same exact thing 500x. It takes a lot of talent these days to make original/modern stories and you are too stupid to have that register in your teeny tiny brains.  For those that say there is nobody to root for? If you really need to root for someone, there is Belinda, the spa lady. I am so sick of people that don't know anything about writing not being able to see great writing when it hits them in the head.  Ok, I had to get that off my chest because I can't stand these haters. I cannot remember the last time I saw something so relevant to the world we are living in right now. It captures our lives at this moment to a T. Mike White has jumped to a new level with this masterpiece that will for sure win a lot of awards.

I gave it a 6 because yes it's fantastic acting, cinematography, and score is all there. But this was some of the most anti climactic nonsense I have ever seen. You sit at the edge waiting for the big twist or turn and it falls flat at every turn. I was entertained to an extent but overall very disappointing. Also the lack of humor in this "comedy" is the funniest part of this show.

Well, Mike White, I think you had the right idea at one-and-done with The White Lotus. Season 1 was deliciously savage class satire, rich with brutal takedowns and dark little laughs. Every week the tensions and discomfort built, till you knew it absolutely, positively *would* get even worse.  And, ooh, those Hawaiian sunsets behind all the snark and yearning!  Season 2 is just flat. A bore. For all the great casting and the history and beauty of Italy, you can only get hit over the head with the dis-pleasures of sex so much (as leverage, as addiction, for money, reeking of desperation, for revenge, incoherently wasted, impotent), before you tire of getting hit. And, this may be personal preference-but dangling one dead body in the opening minutes is more interesting than a passel.

Just like a soap opera there are multiple stories intertwined in a span of a week. It's as interesting as a train wreck in that you can't stop looking knowing that it ends badly.  But for a comedy I never laughed and this is more like a dramedy.

That is 100% masterpiece but not for everyone. I do understand why some people do not get it because there are so many meanings and ideas are being hidden underneath. I haven't seen anything like this for ages, the cast is stunning, the music I would say the best soundtrack of the year, costumes, location and script are awesome too! Truly one of the best show this year, to avoid any spoilers, I would only say it is a beautiful story about pretty common existence issues of all of us. Highly recommended if you are into fragile(in a good way), meaningful and deep series.

If you're going into season 3 with similar expectations as the previous seasons , I would reconsider these thoughts.  Not to say that this latest season didn't have quality, as we still get a stellar new cast, cinematography, atmosphere and vibe which will be a bit familiar from when we visited the hotels from last seasons (characters having more going on then meets the eye). However the bigger pieces of drama do take a lot longer to ramp up - so if you're expecting similar momentum in build up then the first few episodes may end up being a turn off.  One of my favourite aspects of the series is the "who done it" factor, it makes it more thrilling trying to put pieces together to try and guess who might bite the dust at the end of the season and how. Though this season I felt this part of the show didn't really click the same.

Make no mistakes dear reading this review. This show is funny, but at the same time its not?  I liked this show, with a lot of great actors and actresses and more greatness with the script (witch i hated sometimes).  The main problem, it was a bit cringe, and that's fine when you have a comedy show with a 20 episode 20 minutes or something like that. But you cant have a cringe episode in a 6 episodes show, its just not acceptable to waist such potentials.

After seeing that this show had been nominated for a lot of emmys, I decided to give it a watch. I seen that it's an acquired taste type of show, but I was willing to give it a watch, since it's only 6 episodes long.  The White Lotus is painfully average. The entire show feels pointless by the end of it, and pretty much every single character is unlikable, apart from; Jennifer Coolidge and Alexandra Daddario. The rest of the cast are all just boring, and don't get me started on the character Paula - that idiotic and irritating character is the worst thing since Rose in the Last Jedi.  The actual stories themselves are uninteresting, aside from the newly married couple. They have the only story that doesn't feel bland, and the only story that actually progresses and develops by the end of it.  The comedy itself isn't that good at all. It's cringe comedy. You will spend half you time groaning at all the nonsense the show tries to make funny. There are a good few funny lines here and there, but it's not enough. This would have best seen as a drama than a dark comedy.  The performances are all good, which is pretty much the saving grace here. The stands outs are Jennifer, Alexandra and Connie. They all have their moments to shine in very powerful and dramatic scenes, which is why this show even gets a 5/10.  This show is not for everyone, and I'm one of them who did not enjoy it. I'm sure some will love this.

This is way to highly rated for a show about nothing, that plays the same song on loop from beginning to end of every episode. Wife was watching it in another room and thought she was watching porn. Very woke as well btw. Watch out.

I love how each characters true selves slowly unfold each episode. I still hate Jennifer Coolidge though. She plays the same character in everything she plays, and definitely didn't need to be brought back for the 2nd season.  I'm only on the fifth episode, and I'm dying to see what happens. I didn't know that Hulu only releases one episode weekly. Are all of the streaming services slowly reverting back to how regular TV was?  Regardless, the show is amazing, and definitely worth tuning in. The worst part is having to wait a whole week to watch another episode! I must've been late to the party last season, bc I binged the whole season in a week, and binged it again before starting this season.

White still has good skills in building stories, his satirical humor can still make me laugh,, Aimee and Manobal really stole my attention, Aimee I like her acting in Sex Education, her acting skill are beyond doubt and for a beautiful thai girl ,her acting is good and flows naturally. Can't wait for the next episode.

The original HBO-Max series White Lotus is fantastic. I highly recommend you watch all the seasons; season one from Hawaii, season two from Italy, and season three which is now currently airing which takes place in Thailand.  This review will pertain to season three which so far three episodes have aired and it has been fantastic. This is must see TV the first few episodes averaged about 3.5 million viewers which is unheard of for cable TV & streaming! The cinematography, the locales, the casting, the dialogue is all fantastic! I highly recommend you get HBO-Max and begin to watch these shows. These shows are better than 99% of the movies that are playing out in the theater or on other streaming services.  This season of White Lotus, which takes place in Thailand centers around three main storylines; the wealthy Ratliff family from North Carolina featuring a husband, a wife and three kids; a trio of three Caucasian girlfriends who grew up together but are now living separate but are reuniting for a girls trip; and the mysterious Rick and his girlfriend Chelsea who are vacationing at the White Lotus...  There are some very entertaining and great acting performances here from the above mentioned storylines...  Other major plot lines include Belinda the spa manager from White Lotus season one who is now doing some type of a training seminar at the White Lotus in Thailand and also the enigmatic Greg/Gary who was in seasons one and two and now appears in season three in Thailand. There is also a plot regarding two of the intriguing local employees that work at the White Lotus in Thailand, including real life pop star Lisa and actor Tayme Thapthimthong...  I am not going to give away specifics on the show. I want everyone to enjoy this fantastic miniseries!  There are only eight episodes here for White Lotus in Thailand. Each episode is approximately one hour long so the season will go by quickly. We are now entering into episode number four.  I hope you all enjoy White Lotus, as I said before I would start with season one, then season two, then begin watching season three.  Take care and enjoy! Brad P in Cleveland.

I absolutely love this show and have been looking forward to this season. Watching the first episode so far I wasn't disappointed. Actually looking forward to getting more insight into the characters! I heard there was an up and coming actress that joined the cast too and I am impressed by her too. She is a natural and the dialogues didn't feel forced from her.  I liked that we got a glimpse of every character's personality and it gives us a glimpse into what could happen to them if they are not careful. I am interested to see the development of all the characters.  Looking forward to the next episodes.

However, on a mundane night in, I thought I'd check out season 2, and I was floored, I absolutely loved it. This series is nothing like we've ever seen before, every season has a new cast, a new location, and a new hotel.  Every season the storylines are always so great and interesting, as are the characters and their relationships.  They could really keep this series going for as long as they want to, 10 seasons at least. There are so many cities they could set it in, so many actors they could use, and infinite amount of stories of characters they could create.  Every time a new season comes out I get incredibly exited because of the new characters, the new location, and the new cast.  Currently I'd rank the seasons as follows,  1. Season 2 2. Season 1 3. Season 3  Overall, this series is just exceptional and all the seasons and episodes are incredibly entertaining.

Obviously, the characters are annoying and snobby. That's the point. However, the only reason I kept watching was to see who died. (I heard whispers someone died) and otherwise would have missed besides one small question buried in the first episode. If you missed it, you really wouldn't have a reason to watch. Music was over the top obnoxious. Only two characters I was rooting for didn't pan out well. Disappointing watch. Kind of a time sink for very little movement plot-wise. Also, sometimes weird and awkward? While the acting was good, it just wasn't engaging enough for me to suffer through due to little plot development. Props to the hotel manager and his spiraling. That was the best plot line of the otherwise mundane show.

Best show ever! Plots, sup-plots, plot twists are all great. Every single dialogue line is well written, intelligent, funny. Social critique is spot on. Just the right balance between in-your-face and subtlety (unlike the gross, over the top Triangle of Sadness, which I wish I could unsee). All actresses and actors are doing an amazing job! Jennifer Coolidge is the cherry on top. Best music score I've ever seen in a show (or movie). Creative, fun, innovative, intelligent. You can hear the inner jokes in the background music without even being into music, or being a music professional. The opening credits in both season 1 and 2 are genius. If you like shows that are more about the internal then the external you should give this a try. A group of wealthy privileged people arrive at The White Lotus a resort for the wealthy in Hawaii. Each of the characters think they are happy but each one of them quickly starts going through what amounts to an Existential Crisis.  If you want a show with likeable characters this isn't really it. Most of the characters especially in the beginning start out very unlikeable but through the six episodes of the series you actually do find out why they act the way they act.  Still this is worth the watch especially since it is only six episodes.

This show is amazingly well written; boring and a yawn to some, but not at all for me.  I think the thing I appreciated most was that -among this assortment of unlikable characters- as soon as you begin to dislike one, they redeem themselves is some small way and another presents themselves with some seemingly irreconcilable quality... And the best part is: by the end of it, there was no absolute verdict to be given on any one storyline --a strong facet was given to each side of every dynamic/relationship/conclusion in this show and we are free to judge these characters however we see fit! No patronization or forced-feeding; incredible; we are completely able to be our own observers in this show, and that doesn't seem to happen very much any more.  Excellent, true to life, and very different to any other show I've ever seen. Thoroughly enjoyed!

Whether you like the stories or not, there's no denying the mastery behind The White Lotus. You feel transported inside the White Lotus hotels, spying on the obscenely rich holidayers who form the main characters of the show.  Beautiful locations, gorgeous frames, top notch acting and masterful direction makes it feel almost like a reality show.  The two seasons are thematically different. The first, set in Hawaii, is about class/money. Unlike most viewers, I preferred the first season. It takes a good look into how money affects human relationships. Much of the story is best summed up by the quote from Great Gatsby about the rich: "they smashed up things and creatures and then retreated back into their money or their vast carelessness...and let other people clean up the mess they had made."  The second season is set in Sicily and is about sex. The setting is appropriate -- the tales of lust, romps and adultery have a European flavor. The story about two couples who come to vacation together is the best. Meghan Farhy's incredibly well written and well acted character steals the show. The rest of the threads don't quite have the same originality or character development as that one(or the threads of the first season). Some of the stories and characters felt underdeveloped and almost redundant (esp the grandfather and the father).

Plush, expensive resorts. Several plot lines. Some funny. Some dramatic. A good mixture. Season one us set somewhere I'm Hawaii. Number two in Italy. Both are Ship of Fools kind of stories. The second one, at present in its 3rd episode is heading toward a series of murders.

If there was an 11 rating I would have given it.

The White Lotus is certainly compelling television. It is full of terrible human beings doing awful things to each other. The first season built tension better than most dramas in recent memory and while it was often hard to watch for that reason it navigated the line between real life and entertainment quite well. Sadly, the second season lacked all of these virtues. I think the outrageous nature of the story lines in the first year flowed organically whereas in year two, they felt contrived and forced. Even the trademark landscape transitions, while overly bloated, were beautiful in Hawaii, but seemed mostly CGI in Italy. The failures of season two are likely a byproduct of the first season being very popular and HBO wanting to capitalize off of that popularity. Unfortunately, it doesn't appear Mike White had a strong idea for the follow up and that made it fall flat. This type of thing happens to a lot of shows that no one expected to blow up. It was also disappointing that the only character to return was Jennifer Coolidge's Tanya. Everyone loves the actor, so I'm sure she was popular and that made them want her to be the lynch pin for the series. Unfortunately, I found her story line to be the least interesting in both seasons. The first season is absolutely worth a watch and it will likely hoodwink you into going straight into season two like it did with me. Hopefully you will have more fun with it than I did.

I liked Season 1 slightly better because it has a tighter narrative structure, without any scenes that feel unnecessary or boring. The same is not true of Season 2, but I enjoyed that too, regardless. Although I really liked Jennifer Coolidge's performance as the vulnerable and dysfunctional rich heiress, by Season 2, I felt that I have already seen everything about her character and her continued presence was a bit unjustified and felt repetitive.  Both seasons take place in beautiful resorts, and the cinematography and the soundtrack both sometimes feel a bit over the top, as if they were trying to create a film advertising these places (I wouldn't be surprised if Sicily was inundated by American tourists next year as a result, for example).  What is the role of having rich white people as the main characters? Well, I think it is similar in this sense to Big Little Lies, because first, the characters' enviable life and the beautiful scenery add to the enjoyment of the viewer, and second, because by depicting a life of leisure, there are plenty of opportunities for exploring the protagonists' dysfunctionalities (which is more difficult, of course, if your characters are struggling for survival). In Season 1, there are also some threads dealing with social issues and how the different generations handle them (e.g. The conflicts between the rich friend and the poor friend who identifies with the 'oppressed' Hawaiians). Young people are shown to be more socially sensitive but often hypocritical or clueless about the consequences of their actions. Season 1 also presents how a pretty young woman who is from a poor family and feels mediocre as a journalist struggles against the role of being a trophy wife (excellent performance by Alexandra Daddario). In Season 1, there is also more attention given to conflicts between the rich guests and resort employees, particularly the hotel manager. In Season 2, being rich is only explored inasmuch as becoming the target of scams or plots targeting their money. The Italian prostitutes are depicted as quite immoral but still, I felt that the creators showed them in quite a favorable light (young and vivacious, scamming people only because they try to make a living, too).  Masculinity and desire are an important theme in Season 1, too, but are the main focus of Season 2. In Season 1, the young geek discovers male camaraderie and the appeal of the non-virtual world. His estranged parents (dominant mother and emasculated father) find each other again as a result of a dangerous situation. Season 2 takes an honest look at desire and draws the conclusion that accepting not knowing everything about your partner and even some jealousy can spark desire, whereas being too familiar can kill desire. I thought this conclusion was quite insightful but unusual for an American series, which normally have a more puritanical view of the world. The presentation of the three generations of men (boys will be boys) seemed quite conservative in the sense that it treats male desire as a biological given, as non-negotiable (and the young guy, trying to behave differently from his father and grandfather initially, is presented as clueless and pathetic). Although all characters are flawed, the gay characters are even more immoral and promiscuous. I wouldn't go as far as to say that the series is homophobic, but it certainly gets very close.

I came to this series late considering it's in its third season and I'd just finished the first.  I was intrigued by the cast and the positive reviews from critics and viewers.  I have to say that the energy of the series from beginning to end strikes me as a great success.  One episode a day, four dynamics told simultaneously with great fluidity.  Broken, imperfect, self-serving, envious, flawed characters. We see all of this throughout the six episodes that make up this season.  What did happen to me was that as the season progressed, I found the stories less and less engaging. While I was entertained, I couldn't really connect.  We have some very good performances, some overacted, and some risqué scenes, but as I said, the dynamic entertained me.  The final episode was the one I found the least compelling; we had ridiculous conflict resolutions and key characters were no longer seen.  For all these reasons, I consider this first season to be good, but not brilliant.  We'll see what I think of the next ones, but my initial rating would be a 7.

I completed the first season on a binge watch over the course of two days. The last series I did that with was with the first two seasons of Dexter. This series is almost as good but without all the blood and guts of that drama.  Hawaii provides a spectacular backdrop for the story of wealthy people vacationing at a luxurious resort run by a guy who reminded me of Basil(John Cleese) of the great TV comedy Fawlty Towers. He must bow to the whims of a cast of spoiled, self indulgent guests who have no empathy for anyone but themselves.  The cast is awesome and the scripts filled with a biting satire rarely found in today's shows.  The music is also perfect but be forewarned of some cringeworthy moments along the way.  The second season was even better than the first as we get a new cast with only two actors returning from the first season. The plot is again a wild one and the less said, the better in order not to spoil the show.  A third season is planned and I will be there for it. Take the ride.

The White Lotus (season 1)  The first season of The White Lotus opens with a very character driven approach. Each character is fleshed out and developed at a steady pace; the characters are very diverse in their nature, and audiences should find at least one to latch onto. For the most part, the characters are not good or evil, heavily nuanced and gray is what most of them are. The cast that portrayed these characters also deliver a splendid take, with great acting that finding a weak link would prove difficult.  The plot of this is poised to build with mounting tension, and it's built steadily, but the letdown is the finale, it isn't worthy of the tenuous buildup that led to it. The first episode is gripping as it should leave audiences guessing as to how the story proceeds, and as the white Lotus slowly unfolds, it's quite disappointing how it wraps up. It's nice though that there are no loose ends, or at least any that'll leave a bad taste.  The location, setting and cinematography is very pleasing, but much praise must be given to the score.  The White Lotus is enjoyable, especially its characters, and that alone is enough to get audiences through.

I concur with the numerous reviews that highlight the exceptional casting and writing in seasons one and two. Each season introduces characters whose lives intersect and intertwine in unexpected ways, akin to the movie Crash set in a resort setting.  Each season begins gradually, introducing characters who leave clues that lead you down intricate character revelations that culminate in an exhilarating climax.  However, season three has fallen short. Despite a talented cast including Jason Isaacs, Carrie Coons, Michelle Monaghan, and Walter Goggins, the show has failed to deliver. While season three connects characters to season two, there is a noticeable lack of momentum. I've already finished watching episode five, and I'm thoroughly bored.  This is particularly disappointing considering there are only three more episodes left in this season for the show to salvage its reputation.  If you're new to the series, be warned that season three pales in comparison to the previous seasons.  I dropped my original overall rating to 5 stars based on the complete failure of season 3.

I loved this show and wished it didn't have to end. When you look at all the different relationships and what they meant, you can see that this is definitely not a "surface" type of a show. Each relationship has a concept that challenges your personal perspective on what is happening and helps you to think about where each characters perspective is. It deals with subject matters such as class and character development; who you are, where you are, and where you may like to be.  I liked the end. I was a little confused but ultimately I think it was meant to show us that when these characters were taken out of their immediate home environment, their mind was occupied by the realities of the world around them, and they had to confront how they felt about it. They recognized where they were positioned in life, tried to challenge it, and ultimately accepted it for what it was.

I grew up in Hawaii starting back in 1965 at the age of ten then moved to the mainland in 1982. I go back home each year to see my family and friends and to reconnect with the land and culture I hold close to my heart.  This said, I am impressed by the authentic references about Hawaii. Some are obvious while others are subtle but noticed.  Love the song selections from 70s/80s contemporary Hawaiian musicians. Quinn on the beach tripping on whales breaching and observing the outrigger team ritual/camaraderie upon landing, very accurate. Kai's speech about the family land - their aina - was nicely done.  Kudos to the creators for doing this.

Okay, after seeing Season 3, I can confidently say: this is the best TV series I've ever watched. By far. Period.  It's the story, it's the pacing, it's the casting, it's the performances, it's the sets and ambiences - but above all, it's the sheer visual quality of the cinematography and the visual mise-en-scène.  I am completely baffled. Every take feels thought-out, curated, and executed to a level that I simply cannot understand how it's even achievable. How can visual artistry reach a point where, without being obtrusive to the flow of the story or self-indulgent to the point of spoiling the overall experience-something that often happens when cinematography tries to upstage other elements of storytelling - it instead creates a master's tableau in every scene?... A pictogram we want to revisit over and over until we fully grasp its conceptual meaning?  Do the cinematographer, director, and all the other visual artists behind this series spend countless hours outlining, conceptualizing, and implementing these elaborate, yet incredibly fluid, takes? I simply don't understand-but to me, it works like an addiction. And I can hardly wait for Season 4.

The best thing about season 3 is no more Jennifer Coolidge. She plays a version of the same character in every role she takes. She seems to be the type of actress that people either love or hate. I find a little goes a long way. She doesn't steal scenes so much as she elbows the other actors out of the way to be the center of attention.  Season 2 was an improvement. I enjoyed the Sicilian setting. Gorgeous views and a gorgeous cast. The story was more varied and the characterizations were superbly done.  Season 3 is, as some reviewers remarked, a long, uneventful slog that seems to go nowhere. With 3 episodes left, I'm hoping Mike White picks up some steam and delivers a satisfying ending. He's certainly capable of it.  At least I don't have to put up with Coolidge chewing up the scenery yet again.

It's way deeper than you think, absolutely not boring if you can sit in place and pay attention to your fictional life & dreams, together with tremendous writing & directing by the enthusiastic and talented director Mike White.  Awaiting season 2 with anticipation! Hope it's darker and more "pumped-up" though... -------------------------------------------------  Season 3: Welcome to the new White Lotus series and movie altogether. Some times after season 2, in the course of 2023, it dawned on Mike White, what if I made a show and movie as a combo he thought; he had the feeling that he was fed up with the too big of a success of his trademark White Lotus seasons 1 and 2 and thought to himself it would be great to tone down the upcoming season 3 of which he had a vague idea of life & death in Buddhism, soporific Thailand resort on Lorazepam and poisonous fruits that he had no idea yet what to do with them, but like a good Agatha Christie novel he was sure that he would find the true purpose of the fruit in time.  The seed of season 3 was planted then and in the course of several months and many vivid dreams, he completed his journey so dear to his heart and thought to himself with a smirk, how many viewers would go bald prematurely by so pulling their hairs.  I have now realized that HBO needed to first show us episode 8 and after a week provide us with the other episodes for whoever is interested in comatose die-hard backstories, micro orgies and developments.  What a brilliant epiphany you had Mr. White. I bow to you!  Just please, in a binge-worthy season 4, resuscitate Tanya, bring back Chloe, Saxon and Mook with a new resort manager of the big gabarit of Armond the star.  P. S. What you did with that season 3 was a huge disservice to the fans and next time on set, beware of those sharp-tooth baboons. Applicable to season 1. 8.5/10  The White Lotus is a dark tragicomic satire zooming in on the socioeconomic divide between the native population, the working class, and the upper echelons of society.  The White Lotus, a luxurious resort, is build on the stolen lands of native Hawaiians. Not only are their lands stolen, natives are deemed to perform their ancient rituals to please rich guests. At the outside, the lives of these guests seems perfect, but we soon learn they are deeply flawed and superficial.  In my opinion, the performances of Jennifer Coolidge (as Tanya, confused and out of touch) and Murray Bartlett (as Armond, the manic hotel manager) carry The White Lotus. I look forward to season 2.

One of the best shows to be ever made truly. The intensity the grit the mystery the romances and the whole concept of rich white family dynamics on vacation is just most extraordinary visual presentation. Beautiful performance by LITERALLY every single cast members including extras haha , HIGH RESPECT AND PRAISE AND LOVE TO MIKE WHITE, He has done a tremendous job directing writing producing (kinda wish he starred in this too!!) Both seasons so far have explored Hawaii and Italy and I am beyond glad they have renewed for a third season looking forward to seeing what's the next destination! CANT WAIT.

Mike White is a good storyteller and always has good characters. This season was no different except for the situations he put them in. It was much darker than the past two seasons and some of the scenes are uncomfortable. But that's probably what he was going for, and if so, it worked. Walter Goggins was good, but the scene stealer in this one is Parker Posey. She was great as the mother of a dysfunctional family. Is an award in her future? I think so. They bring back some characters from the past and seamlessly bring them into the storyline. The setting in Thailand is great and the camera work around scenes creates a cool vibe. Definitely not for the faint of heart, but worth watching.

I cant say that i had high hopes for this one but i had run out of things to watch, i would usually go with something a little grittier but oh did i love it and finished it in one wet and windy day (annual leave of course). It was such a good watch. The cast were incredible, it all came together really well.  Great storyline set over 1 week in Hawaii following the guests and the hospitality staff. Having worked in hospitality for the majority of my working life it showed a true reflection of just how much you have to put up with from these types of guests, very entertaining.  Brilliantly done & outstanding acting. My favourite character of all had to be Jennifer Coolidge as Tanya, she literally cracks me up and plays this type so perfectly.  Put this on your watch list and give it a try, by the time it finishes you'll be wanting season 2!!

So this show was very good and at times was slow burn is worth the watch. For each character it's like you rooting for a wanted good outcome for the character and might get what you want but in exchange for something you don't want for the character. Like a deal with the devil. This is a sinful show so got to be ok with watching it and can be a mindfu$$ too. It's got a Revenge tv show and Murder on the Orient Express movie feel of suspense and mystery. I highly recommend this show so pay attention. You will enjoy it.
