Season 1: The music was so distracting I watched a lot using captions, sound off. It was like funeral music. This season would have had more appeal without it. Season 1 is set in Hawaii, so the set is beautiful. The story line weaves through all 6 episodes, ending with the 6th one.  Season 2 is set in Sicily with better music. Same format (7 episodes), more beautiful locations.  Both are entertaining dramedies. Each character has their own quirks and dysfunction and their interactions with each other throughout the seasons are what the series is about. I think of it as a 6-7 episode murder mystery. Season 2 also has unappealing music in the finale, too distracting and takes away from enjoying the show.  Best quote: (Daphne to Harper) "You don't have to know everything about someone to love them"

White Lotus season 1 & 2 were fantastic. I throughly enjoyed the comedic relief, build up and the characters on the other seasons. This season nothing has happened. We're halfway through the season and there's no likable characters, the incest plot is gross, the friend group is somewhat interesting. Mook and the security guards storyline, boring and he's just dumb for leaving that gun out. The Ratliff family are weirdos. The dad has been high as a kite and no one has noticed. The wife is the only character who adds a sense of comedic relief to the show. This season has fell short and I don't think it'll get better. Every time I think we're getting somewhere the episode ends and I feel like I'm in the same spot as I was in episode 1. This season is purely hype I'm beyond disappointed with this garbage of a season.

Absolutely loved this. Quirky, original, perceptive and real. A character study of small lives and the utter banality and boredom bred by privilege. These characters are the centre of their universe and have little regard for anyone or anything else. Some moments were hilarious, others touching, heartbreaking and thought provoking. It's so utterly of our time but the questions it raises are timeless. A masterpiece!

Fell in love with this from episode 1, real problems, make believe, it is just REAL and most of it relatable.  I am almost certain there is an Armond lurking somewhere in the Hospitality industry and I am dying to meet him with my myriad booking problems LOL.  Tanya McQuoid, what all broken promises are made of, incredible.  Paula, what can I say, how quickly can a person turn.  Can't wait for season 2 .

Both Seasons One and Two are compulsively watchable primarily because Mike White accurately captures the zeitgeist of wealthy entitlement in situations that bring out the worst in his characters. He also understands his actors well and allows them room to go off the deep end with the desperate people they play. Season Two in Sicily reflects this skill even more effectively than Season One in Hawaii - even though both story arcs revolve around the same leitmotif of the discovery of a dead body. Jennifer Coolidge carries over her whacked-out character, Tanya McQuoid, from one season to the next. The various storylines still revolve around privilege and self-justified deception, but somehow White hits harder in Season Two with a deeper sense of fatalism and a darker tone of black comedy with an even sharper cast that includes a surprisingly effective Aubrey Plaza.

White Lotus is one of the best, sharpest and most consistently funny satires I've ever seen. It takes on the preening privileges of the moneyed class as they vacation at White Lotus resorts.  So far we've seen the Maui and Italy hotels, but no doubt they extend worldwide for more fun & games, with a different resort featured. Each season begins with the implication that a character has died, and the episodes are a flashback to how it happened.  It's hard to top the epic hilarity of the wildly dysfunctional Mossbacher family from season 1, not to mention with the ongoing battle between the fed-up manager Armond vs Sean, the toxic male Karen. Season 2 is somewhat less funny but has a more structured murder-mystery.  The cast largely changes with each season but I've heard that a character from season 1 will be back for season 3.

The White Lotus definitely has a unique vibe - gorgeous locations, sharp direction, and a cast that really brings the characters to life. There's this slow-burn tension throughout that kept me watching, and the social satire is smart in places.  But at the same time, it felt like it was almost great. Some of the storylines dragged or fizzled out, and a few characters felt more like caricatures than real people. The pacing can be slow, and while the awkward humor works at times, it also left me a bit underwhelmed.  Still, it's visually beautiful and has moments of brilliance. Worth watching if you like slow, character-driven drama with a satirical edge - just don't expect it to be as deep or biting as it sets itself up to be.
Specifically throat cancer so they can't talk ever again. Ever.

I don't even know what this show was supposed to be.. it's listed as a comedy, but I didn't laugh a single time. I kept waiting for it to get interesting, but it never did.. I'm actually upset I wasted 6 hours of my life on this crap. There's truly not a single thing I liked about it.. maybe Alexandra Daddario, she's the only saving grace. And it's also supposed to be a murder mystery?? Uhh not really.. you hear in the beginning that someone died, and then find out in the last episode who, and it was so anticlimactic and pointless!!!!! I was expecting the whole show to have the murder mystery element in there, but no... so lame, truly one of the worst shows I have seen. I will most definitely be skipping the second season without hesitation!

The White Lotus is a deliciously dark satire that hooked me from the first episode and didn't let go until the credits rolled on the season finale. This series isn't just another vacation drama; it's a captivating exploration of privilege, class, and the complexities of human relationships.  The stunning backdrop of the luxurious White Lotus resorts provides a stark contrast to the unraveling lives of its guests. The ensemble cast is phenomenal, each actor embodying their flawed and multi-layered characters with remarkable depth. The dialogue is sharp, witty, and often brutally honest, making for some truly memorable moments.  While the series has its fair share of comedic moments, it also delves into darker themes, exploring the often toxic dynamics between the wealthy and the people who cater to their every whim. It's a show that doesn't shy away from social commentary, offering a biting critique of modern society's obsession with status and materialism.  The writing is exceptional, with each episode expertly building tension and suspense. The plot twists are unexpected, and the ending is both satisfying and thought-provoking. "The White Lotus" is a masterclass in storytelling, and I highly recommend it to anyone looking for a series that's both entertaining and intellectually stimulating.

This HBO MAX series is not very well acted; shot in a color unknown on planet Earth; has an erratic story line; and features music better suited for Indonesia than Hawaii. Nonetheless, since Hawaii was our favorite place (until it was overrun by people much like these) we gave it a watch. It is just (barely) campy enough to keep a viewer watching.
Two episodes in and I fully don't understand what this show is about. Everyone except 2 characters are horrible people. There is nothing funny or entertaining about this show.

Wow, I haven't liked a show this much in a long time, and the funny fact is, I don't even know WHY I like it so. When you get right down to it, viewers of The White Lotus are little more than voyeurs watching the daily intricacies of various human lives play out at a couple of the nicest resorts in the world. I got so hooked on these sneak peeks into the swank hotel rooms of these strangers, I'm a little deflated now that it's all over.  In my book, there is not a single thing that this show doesn't do right. The acting is top shelf. The character development is flawless, the dialogue is perfect and every little human flaw is examined at on almost uncomfortable level. Obviously the cinematography is next level and the stories are perfectly paced.  Season 2 surprised me a little in that an actual plot appeared out of nowhere. I thought we were just enjoying the tawdry interactions of the characters like before - and believe me, I was happy with that - and then BAM! What do you know? A couple dark twists and we've got a real drama on our hands.  I don't agree with those who say this show features nothing but rich people problems. The kinds of woes these people suffer through are of the same variety all of us experience because we are flowed and complicated creatures. These storytellers could set their next series on the bad side of a depressed former mill town and I'll bet they can make it sing.  Won't be as pretty, though.

Hollow, shallow human souls. It is difficult to get sympathy for any of them, with one, maybe two, exceptions.  After the first episode, I wanted to throw the TV out the window. Did not want to spend more time with these no good people.  But like many of the great works, it starts with pain, is slow and strange, but suddenly it loosens up and it is impossible to stop until you see the end credits of the last episode. For me, it happened about halfway into the second episode.  Masterful!

A comedy of grief and expectation - the characters in this are so well written and the Intertwining stories add to their complexity. Almost feels like it was written for a stage play with the one location. Even though they've pushed the envelope on the characters flaws I still would have like to have seen more, nevertheless some great moments in each episode... bring on season 2.

Just when I was about to say this is my new favorite TV show, I watched the second season and I am so disappointed. The new characers are way less interesting, and it's as if everyone is driven by their horniness. Seriously did the writers think it's a good idea to revolve the plot around 2 pr*stitutes?.  The unnecessary sex scenes make it boring and it feels like they ran out of ideas. It's as if the team behind the production just wanted to see these actresses flash their t*ts.  The conflicts of the characters are just not as equally interesting for me to buy them unlike in season 1. In the second season, it's like everyone is just struggling with handling their libido and it keeps happening on the show. I really wish the writer becomes more inspired for the next season because I'm so disappointed with the downgrade that season 2 is.

The cinematography, acting, and dark comedy are on point here. However, these factors cannot overcome a piss poor plot and racist undertones. The plot is so high level there isn't any room for character development and frankly who really cares when you're dealing with characters who are written to be despised; double negative. The viewer needs to care, otherwise what's the point.

This series looks so mainstream yet it is so surprising at the same time. The smart storyline makes you expect things to happen because the outcome of situations leads obviously to what you think, yet other things happen. It's hilarious in it's own strange way. The acting is superb. Some situations magnify things in life that are recognisable and tragic at the same time, when you realize that those things actually are all around you. Rich people exploiting poor by throwing them expectations then dumping them. Additions that brings the bad out of actual good persons. The surface of the fake smile from hotelpersonel with loads of troubles hidden behind it. Spoiled rich kids who doesn't realize how feeble and fragile they actually are, protected by mom and dad's dollars. It's tragic, recognisable and hilarious all together. I would vote to get more like this on screen. I seldom write reviews but this one is really worth it. Start watching without expectations, just go for the ride and let it all sink in. You will not regret. Oh, and it's also very bingeable. Enjoy your stay in the White Lotus hotel.

Ultimately, in season two of White Lotus was extremely disappointing. They had fashioned these characters to where we actually cared about them, and then had them do awful and disappointing things across-the-board. The message of the stories generally were about relationships are at their base just mutual using situations where sometimes one prevails well over the other and other times, relationships are about settling for what you can get.  The decisions that the characters make are seen through the visor of who is being naïve, and who is taking care of that, nativity. In the end, all of the characters suffer that have a naïve trait, and those who are seeking to settle or take advantage of that nativity are shown to triumph across all of the relationships depicted in the show. All of the scenes are well acted and the cast does a great job with the Plot line they are given.  At one time or another all of the characters elicit a visceral reaction to their poor behavior, poor decisions, and sometimes lack of action until it's too late. As a viewer at the end of the episodes, one is left with a feeling of heavy disappointment in the decisions that are made, and the empty relationships all of the characters are left with.  One thing of note is the photography of the spectacular locations. Sicily and other parts used in the filming come off extremely well. One will be tempted to immediately purchase a ticket to Palermo, or to other parts of Sicily to enjoy the combination of ancient architecture and rolling beautiful countryside while mount Etna rumbles above it all.  This well, active drama leaves a thudding emptiness in the viewer like the unsatisfying relationships. Each of the characters is left with as they settle for what they can get or what they can tolerate. This is a great result, because it had to be the aim of the writers, producers and actors. And they deliver.

Completely terrible. Characters are so unlikeable, unredeemable and unwatchable. There is not one character in this entire series that is bearable to watch. Only surprised I watched the entire six episode season.

I binge watched this tv show in just two days because it was made to be very addictive with ethereal music, beautiful scenery, perfect scripting and character development. It was just such treat that I forgot everything else.  Characters are very interesting, multidimensional and none of them are underdeveloped. That along with alluring music takes the show to another level.  Second season was a lot sexier than the first, of course left me with a thought that there had been some temporary loss of ideas. However it turned out better than I had expected.  The plot itself is fairly simple and it is repeated on the second season. I believe that repeating the plot is going to wear after such a spectacular finale of the second season. It felt like a good point for a conclusion but as it happens this thing is going to get renewed.

The White Lotus is an entertaining limited series about a group of guests (and a few employees) at a Hawaiian resort over the course of a week. Now that doesn't sound very exciting, even with a stellar cast.  However, the character development is outstanding. The show, while a satirical comedy, digs deep to create emotional characters and challenge long-held cultural beliefs (even if it isn't entirely successful).  The standout here is Armond (Murray Bartlett) as the hotel manager. He's slick with the guests, but like many of the employees, desires more than meeting the needs of rich white people. The performance is over-the-top and magical at the same time. It's complemented by thoughtful costuming.  Costuming throughout is fantastic and (mostly) very stylish. It reveals so much about each character.  The White Lotus is a tropical vacation worth taking.
I am hooked! Phenomenal cast but Jennifer Coolidge steals the show. Still amazing performances all round. So mysterious and quirky. Can't wait for season 2.

A show trying to be deep and failing utterly. The script was weak, the dialogue was terrible - and it was definitely not witty like people have been saying, quite the opposite, in fact. Uninteresting characters for whom you feel no shred of emotion whatsoever, never mind any empathy or sympathy.  I watched the whole season, waiting to see the brilliant comedy and dry wit that everyone kept gushing about. But I only disliked it more and more with every episode.  Overall pointless, boring, and at times unnecessarily disgusting. I genuinely have no idea what people found to like in this show. If I could give it negative stars, I would.

Let me lead with this: if you're looking for laugh out loud funny, you won't get it here. If you want lovable characters, you've come to the wrong place. If you're like me and you're into moral ambiguity and nuanced characters, then okay, go for it. I didn't discover this show till just prior to the start of season 3 and I'm so glad I did. Season 1 is a work of art. I'm a little less crazy about season 2 but I fully appreciate how it fits into the bigger picture. I'm seeing a lot of hate or at least indifference toward season 3 because it's much quieter and significantly slower of a burn, but I'm very into it. For reference I'm writing this just prior to the season 3 finale and I have the utmost faith in a big enough payoff, and that all of my predictions will be wrong. This show wins my personal award for most twists I never saw coming and that in and of itself is pretty spectacular.

The story is amazing, all the actresses are so great especially Lisa. As a debut actress I think she did a great job. Anyway I'm looking forward to see what's coming next and more of Lisa's performance. I'm new for this series but already a big fan and I can't believe that I didn't watch the white lotus series before, such a waste. I'm just obsessed with all the story around rich people and I can't believe I like it. But I heard that there were some shock scenes happened in the pre season it make me worry a little bit but still excited. Overall It is worth watching and those who have not seen it should see immediately.

Why was there so much music this season? Were the first two seasons like that? I don't think so. I found it really distracting and aggravating to the point where I muted the show and just read the subtitles. It almost seemed like the music was being used to evoke the emotions and tone that the actors and directors were responsible for. Other shows use music much more effectively and with less of a heavy hand. I hope the next season does not rely so heavily on music. If so, I will be turning it off as soon as I hear the first set of bongos or wind chimes kick in. I loved the first two seasons but this one was almost unbearable to finish.

I absolutely loved the first episode of the third season! The plot is engaging and full of potential, keeping me hooked from start to finish. The interactions between the cast are simply incredible, making every scene even more captivating. I also find the theme of spirituality fascinating, and I'm excited to see how it will unfold throughout the season. The way all the storylines intertwine adds depth to the narrative, making everything feel connected and meaningful. A special highlight goes to Aimee Lou and Lalisa Manobal, whose performances were outstanding-emotional, powerful, and truly mesmerizing! I'm already counting down the days until next Sunday!
--- Episode 6 !  At series end the show comes across as sophomoric and oh so predictable.  I'm giving 8 stars because the first 5 episodes are fasinating and surprising.

This is a true masterpiece!  I've been binging season 1 & 2 whitin a couple of days and I literally can't stop watching! The show has a lot of twists & turns you won't expect. I love everyone's performance in this show as well!  It's a dark comedy and I've never seen anything like it. I can imagine this show could have infinite seasons and I truly hope they will never stop making new seasons of "The white lotus".  It's a pleasure to watch. I've not seen a boring episode so far and I'm starting season 3 today!  I really love the cinematography and the locations they have used to shoot this series! I'm hoping they'll make a new season in at my favourite Island "Bali" one day'. If not, I'll continue watching anyway ;)

What can I say? First season was pretty good, funny, well acted, interesting to watch. I really enjoyed it and had high hopes that the second one will be at least that good. The reality was brutal and after a first episode I almost slept trying to watch it to the end. But I gave it a chance, basing on the very good experience earlier. No, I just finished 3rd episode and this isn't going to happen. What the hell have they done with this series??? If season 1 was rated 8\10 then season 2 is 3\10! It's like someone with no sense of humor and movie experience took it in his hands and screwed it completely. That's a disaster, a DISASTER. Give my 3 hours of my life back.
Boring, vapid, and soooooo slow. I hung in there convinced it would reveal a link to purpose or hint of entertainment value. It did not.

Dark secrets and twisted truths of the guests, the staff and the locale of a resort are unveiled over the course of a week that was supposed to be a relaxing vacation.  If ever a TV series should've stopped after season 1 and not followed up with a watered down season 2, it's this one.  The characters, plot, humour and atmosphere are very good in season one and the humour is on point. It's a really enjoyable watch and very entertaining. We were invested in the characters and wanted to see what happened next. However, withing 1-2 episodes of season two, we dropped it and haven't gone back. Proof that it's hard to replicate success with a weaker cast, weaker storylines and scripts that aren't as funny.

This show has some nice visuals, exceptional camera work, lovely music and some good acting from at least some actors and actresses but it suffers from lacking a storyline. I am not saying the storyline is bad or weak. I am saying that there is really no storyline at all. Nothing, literally nothing.  The entire show consists of rich people on vacation arguing, bickering and complaining about petty stuff that doesn't even matter to anyone else and there is nothing else going on.  There isn't even a real conflict about anything. For 3 episodes this guy complains on and on about why he was supposed to get the honeymoon suite but got the king suite instead. Then for 3 episodes we hear another character complaining about losing their cell phone and not having a phone. Another character looks really sad and depressed and barely talks 1 word per minute and doesn't even know what she wants.  You just watch a few spoiled people go on vacation and complain about petty stuff like their room or restaurant food for 6 hours with nothing else going on.

I enjoyed some of of it but it was pretty light on the comedy side. Dysfunctional, tragic entitled white folk with mental health issues 'ain't so funny but there were a few good lines but I wouldn't go so far as to say it's a comedy.
They are not easy to find and they are rare..  An all around masterpiece.

Season 3 in Thailand  Kind of a "slice of life" among some wealthy, unfocused, immoral, uninspiring wastrels on vacation in a tropical setting catering to the indolent unsatisfied, on a break from their usual tedious lives in the USA.  You get the feeling the Season is intended to make some serious points about life, with some religious Thai natives explaining the satisfying way to live. However, discipline is not a possible for our holidayers.  It might be that the point of interspersed shots of monkeys in the jungle is intended to illustrate the most creatures can expect from life: don't be too ambitious and enjoy life.  Apparently, philosophy aside, extreme partying it up in Thailand can have a sobering effect upon some of the participants. They apparently conclude that the rewards of hedonism are somewhat limited. Maybe living in the USA where their tendency to excess is a bit more curtailed, so long as you have enough money, you will be able to scrape together a comfortable existence if you don't have deep expectations. Just don't underestimate the value of money.  It's pretty boring. The life lessons to be learned are not subtle, and not actually learned. The simple fact is that the writer/director Mike White has an unrelenting cynicism about life - there are no silver linings and there are no heros. If you find labored, unsuccessful struggle against lack of character entertaining, go for it.

Actors are fabulous! Coolidge being the best! There are only 2 types. Those who hate and those who love it. It seems pretty obvious that those who hate it seem to all feel it's some white people attack. Others like me see characters that are funny as hell ,rich as hell and are terribly flawed. If you don't get annoyed there's something wrong. You are supposed to get annoyed. The music is addicting. It's overall a great show compared to other shows on right now. I gave it an 8. But may up it if I like the ending.

Overall, this is a decent effort wrapped up nicely in a 6 episode package. The most redeeming quality for me was the exceptionally believable characters who actually had intelligent and realistic dialogue and interaction. As the character development is one of the most important parts of a drama of this scope, this already puts it on a solid footing.  Everything else was as expected from an standard HBO production. Quality sound design and soundtrack, good visuals, and solid acting. The storyline could have been a bit more interesting in the end, but I feel it's still a solid effort as well.  Edit: I'm taking this from an 8 to a 9 for season 2, which I felt had a much more deep and tangible set of characters. Although the story was slow at times, I was riveted. Major kudos to the writers.

Fantastic actors Great music and vibe Great writing The character arks and journeys are satisfying Themes such as entitlement, vanity, hedonism, first world problems Only 6 episodes   Another aspect that helped me enormously understand the show, was the behind the scenes insights of each episode. It helps one understand a ton more about the character's motivations and fears in a superb articulated manner. Can't stress that enough.

As a long-time fan of The White Lotus, I approached Season 3 with high expectations, and I was not disappointed. Set in Thailand, this season delves deeper into the complexities of identity, spirituality, and the human condition, all while maintaining the show's signature blend of dark humor and social commentary.  The choice of Thailand as the backdrop was inspired. The lush landscapes, serene temples, and vibrant markets provided a stunning contrast to the internal turmoil of the characters. The cinematography was exceptional, capturing both the beauty and the underlying tension of the setting. The incorporation of Thai rock, pop, and dance music further enriched the atmosphere, enhancing the show's immersive experience.

This show has some of my favourite actors. I can't believe I'm Dying Up Here got cancelled and then this gets green lit.  It reminds me of the american office, just weird, not funny (British original The Office was brilliant and painfully funny).

Very interesting watching these characters interact with eachother. It was a bit heavy handed with the propaganda but if you're able to get through that it is a very cool show. Reminded me of 'Old' but without the horror aspect.

This show is genius. Alexandra's entrance is heart-stopping and the sound track/audio engineering is exceptional.  The main track is an ear worm, but not in an annoying way.  The characters are all developed beautifully and are all dealing with quite complex personal issues, but it is NOT a soap.  Very good fun, right from the start.

In my opinion, the characters remained dislikable or to shallow to carry the story. Actually I waited the whole serie that it would get better or turn around, as the plot and the reviews were quite promising.  The actors did a good job, but so many interactions and dialoges were just to long, over the top, or cringe. Good potential, but character building and development were done unsatisfactory. Not sure if it intended to be a satire? But they didn't achieved that.  But I still watched it to the end to see how it ends, so not totally bad. Watch it if you like nice Hawaii pictures and music, though.

Can't believe I waited for this third series and even paid for a subscription to watch. Loved the first two seasons but this is pure drivel. The plot(s) is noncesical, the characters dislikeable, and aside from the overarching theme that rich people bad, working class good it's no match for the other seasons. Missing comedy, missing appealing characters, even the sound track is repetitive and boring. I've never cared less for characters. Good actors are wasted and watching Patrick Schwarzenegger, Lalisa and the hotel manager will give you splinters.  The acting throughout is dull, the script is grim, the plot ridiculous.  Avoid if you can.
Smart, intelligent and profound charakter study filled with cringeworthy and hilarious moments, on top of the number one theme of our times.

White Lotus,  Mic drop. As an "emerging writer," I often put forward the notion that contemporary fiction would be dull without gay, male novelists (Grant Ginder). And the same may be said of television and Mike White, the writer behind White Lotus. I had my issues with the first and second seasons of White Lotus; I can say that the third season left me feeling satisfied.  Yes, I am biased. I'm from Alabama dealing with family issues. So, oh my god, I needed this season In ways I don't think even the creators, nor my doctor understand. Oh my god I need more wine. Please, I need help. Thanks. Unresolved- I get it now it's a gift to the suffering in Alabama. It is to me at least.

The White Lotus is the least devious of the three resorts if you choose to ignore how convoluted the staff & the guests are. The series is set over the span of a week wherein we are introduced to a group of guests who check-in together at the resort: a dysfunctional family, newly weds & a troubled woman, who is grieving her mother's death. The resort is run by Armond, a recovering drug addict, who appears all cheery but he is short tempered and fuming when is he with the staff or by himself.  The best part about shows or movies set at resorts is the ensemble cast. Season 1 of The White Lotus has a terrific cast that include the likes of Connie Britton, Jennifer Coolidge, Sydney Sweeney, Alexandra Daddario, Steve Zahn, Fred Hechinger, Molly Shannon, Brittany O'Grady, Natasha Rothwell, Jake Lacy & Murray Bartlett as Armond.  The performances are impeccable! Sweeney nails every role she is in. Daddario gets a chance to showcase her talent. Coolidge is a revelation (rumor has it that she is set to reprise her character in season 2). And the best of the lot is Murray's Armond. He starts out as that cheery, positive character but with each passing episode he becomes someone else altogether. The stress of being a manager gets to him.  The White Lotus is one of my favourite shows from 2021. It has a dreamy cast, it is set in the picturesque Hawaii & it keeps you hooked! I don't mind visiting this resort.

Get ready for a captivating and thought-provoking journey with "White Lotus" on HBO Max. This exceptional TV show is a must-watch for anyone looking for something fresh and exciting, featuring captivating characters and exceptional acting that will keep you engaged from start to finish.  What sets "White Lotus" apart is its ability to address complex themes and issues, such as privilege, class, and the dark side of human nature, in a nuanced and thought-provoking manner. The exceptional writing is reflected in the sharp and witty dialogue that adds depth to each character.  Overall, "White Lotus" is an outstanding TV show that should not be missed. The combination of breathtaking cinematography, excellent acting, and masterful storytelling makes it one of the best shows currently available. With two equally great seasons set in different locations, "White Lotus" is a true gem that delivers consistently exceptional quality. It's an 8/10 for me, and I can't recommend it enough.

I really wanted to like season 3. Season 1 felt like a fresh take with some laugh-out-loud moments and fun characters. Season 2 I maybe even enjoyed more. But for me, the bloom has really gone off by season 3.  The 'upstairs/downstairs' contrast is neither as catchy or impactful as the previous seasons and the Agatha Christie-esque moments of the final instalment are telegraphed transparently. Several of the characters and arcs are just as predictable and there are few stand-out performances.  I know lots of viewers are put off by the over-abundance of villains in the White Lotus anthology but it's key to its weird charm. But this set of characters are more hapless than anything else.  And speaking of villains, I'm not sure why Mook is given such a free ride. The fact that she's stunning doesn't make up for her manipulation of poor Gaitok.  I'll look forward to series 4 if there is one, if only to see if the producers can recapture the dark satire of previous seasons and give us something to really talk about other that Walton Goggins, who is good but not great, particularly when played against the marvellous Aimee Lee Wood.
Great atmospheric soundtrack and beautifully filmed. One of the best series I have watched in a long time. The hotel manager was the stand out performance for me.
Quite a cast of characters who are essentially all horrible humans. This attempts to be a dark comedy and potentially social commentary, which more so just ends up being dark without purpose.

The White Lotus (Season 1 & 2) is a series that I recently wrapped up on HBOMAX. The season 1 storyline follows a group of travelers in an exotic hotel in Hawaii. One group at the hotel is an entitled family of conservatives with two children and a friend of the daughter. As the story unfolds there's darkness in the parents past that is bound to resurface. Also on this trip is a recently married couple with the wrong room and the wrong expectations of each other and a woman whose mother recently passed away and is looking for closure.  The season 2 storyline follows a group traveling to an exotic hotel in Sicily including a family traveling with just the dads side of the family due to some recent and ongoing infidelities. The son attends as well to try and give his dad good advice but the grandfather attends offsetting the good advice. There's also a successful business couple from season 1 who struggle with sex and romance and two fraternity brothers who bring their significant others on the trip. Throw in a couple prostitutes into the story and what could go wrong?  At the end of each season...someone is going to die.  The series was created by Mike White (School of Rock and Nacho Libre) and season 1 stars Jennifer Coolidge (American Pie), Jon Gries (Napoleon Dynamite), Connie Britton (Promising Young Woman), Steve Zahn (Joy Ride), Sydney Sweeney (Euphoria) and Jake Lacy (Rampage).  Season 2 stars Jennifer Coolidge (American Pie), Jon Gries (Napoleon Dynamite), F. Murray Abraham (Scarface), Theo James (Divergent), Aubrey Plaza (Dirty Grandpa), Michael Imperioli (The Sopranos) and Sabrina Impacciatore (The Passion of the Christ).  This series has a tremendous Alfred Hitchcock feel to it where it builds up the characters, storyline and various sub plots then has a traumatic murder and who done it element...but they tell you the "why" first then show you the murder. The writing is absolutely outstanding. I have been thoroughly impressed with both seasons characters, circumstances and how the situations methodically unfold. The settings and cinematography is gorgeous. This is a very smart and modern series with throwback elements. I can't wait for season 3.  Overall, this is one of the better new series out there. I would score this a 9/10 and strongly recommend it.

I have really enjoyed this but I think it could do with a little more gravitas behind the characters to make them more believable. Maybe they could have concentrated on less character stories rather than doing half attempts on lots of characters.
The acting, writing and direction are excellent! This is one of the best explorations of some of the societal issues modern America is grappling with today: anxiety, racism, classism, etc.
I love this so far! I was a big fan of Party Down. If you liked it, you'll love this! Obviously, it's not for everyone, but I just can't get enough of it. I hope there are many more seasons to come!

This is such an average show with simple storylines and annoying characters so how the f is it rated higher than The Nevers that is a masterpiece. Are people losing their minds? Or getting too lazy to actually wanna watch something more complex that takes a few views to get a good grasp of what is going on? Because this show have zero rewatch value and sure it has some good messages and a few good moments but come on!

I binge watched this show in a weekend and was gutted when it was over. A fabulous series written - and directed - by Mike White and beautifully crafted into 6 episodes. Accompanied by excellent music too.  The acting was brilliant but I have to say I was particularly impressed by Murray Bartlet (who I'd never seen before - how is this possible?! This guy is SO good!). The other stand out performance for me was Jennifer Coolidge. Also great to see Steve Zahn.  Quirky, dark and gripping. Highly recommend.

My rating averages both seasons. First season was a binge watch. Great script, great acting and really captured the absurdity of what it's like to be in the hospitality business. The second season was significantly duller and less dynamic with a script that had far too many spaces in it. They start both seasons with the first episode hinting at how the season will end which reels the viewer in to watch. I found the second season wasn't as comical as the first and the 2nd season acting was unimpressive with the exception of Coolidge, Richardson and Fahy. Pros of both seasons is that they are filmed on location. In.
Give Jennifer Coolidge her awards! My goodness she is amazing in this role as Tanya McQuoid.

I, like a lot of people have mentioned, found it difficult to like any of the characters, except for Rachel, who is decidedly neutral. It's not that I oppose that aspect, but I just wasn't in the mood for that kind of show. However, I have been sufficiently drawn in by all the insanity, and I have to know what happens next in the various scenarios. Most of all, I need to know who is in that casket we see in the first episode. Considering Shane is the first character we meet, and he is on his honeymoon, yet his wife is not with him, it points to Rachel. But then again, that just seems too easy. Soooo...

I watched this after it won a bunch of Emmy Awards and it was...yeah, not bad. Following a family, a honeymooning couple and single woman all spending a week at a luxury Hawaiian resort, there are enough plot ideas and good performances to keep a viewer interested. It feels a little like a well made, well acted soap opera at times but that might be unfair - it is, after all, satire.. It's amusing and has a dig at modern woke culture and you'll be trying to work out who dies (because the opening scene tells you someone has died), though I felt it petered out in the end. One final thing: okay as it is, it is not on the same planet as Succession, which should have won every Emmy available.

Incredibly booooring-! Wow! Wow!! How could anybody like this? 9 stars? 10 stars!? For this?! What?! I just can't imagine anybody wanting to watch a series with characters that overreacts and gets hung over by such trivial problems. There's no drama or what so ever, the first character which you are supposed to be empathetic about turns out to be an unlikable person right out of the gate, the whole plot is just flat for three consecutive episodes.

This is a great comedic show with good character development. What I enjoyed most with how it showed the upper class characters disregard to the working-class staff. Some of it was contempt and some of it was pure ignorance. But there needs to be more of this on TV so those types of spoilt brats can look inward and treat everyone with respect.

Yeah I liked this show. I just couldn't look away from the carnage. Also because lot's of what is brought up will be recognizable for lot's of people. People who found the characters impossible to like, have a very naive view on humanity or esteem themselves much to high. I liked it because it shows the ugliness and beauty of life and the imperfection of most of us. We just make do with what we have. Do you like watching irritating, passive-aggressive, entitled people get away with everything? This is the show for you.  I wanted to set most of them on fire. It's like browsing twitter or facebook for a couple of hours. Brilliantly done.

Let me preface by saying this - The White Lotus is an incredibly intriguing show. I was captivated after each episode with the exception of the last. The cinematogrophy was exceptional, the sets were well made, and the acting had me immersed.  The glaring flaw this for this series is the inability to tie these characters individual stories together into a cohesive plot. With 10 minutes to go in the final episode I was wondering how they were going to tie up everything with so little time left, well they didn't. It was anticlimactic and disappointing. 7 brilliant episodes amounting to a short and seemingly rushed ending.  Murray Bartlett absolutely steals the spotlight every time he is on the screen. He plays an empathetic and flawed character perfectly and you can't help but root for him even if he isn't a completely good person.  I also enjoyed Steve Zahn's performance, capturing the struggles of a middle-aged man looking only to be respected by his family. I really felt for his character because he genuinely seems to be a good person with a relatively common and relatable problems.  Sydney Sweeney played a believable spoiled brat teenage daughter. I found her reprehensible so I feel like she did her job well.  I believe The White Lotus is worth watching but enjoy each episode for what it is and don't expect a satisfying ending.
Cringe, funny , satire, 10/10. All i can wish for in this type of show.

Very very smart/dark comedy. The rivalry between the resort manager and the rich dude is top notch acting. I found myself laughing throughout most of the episodes. Each character has a running plotline with other resort vacationers and the way their plots intertwine is magnificent. The filming of the show is beautiful as well and if you're anything like me, you will want to upgrade your sunglasses game. The show also gives you vacation MV to the max and will make you wanna book a week at sandals immediately. It took me a long time to try the show, but once you do you will get sucked into this one of a kind show almost instantly.

This show had its interesting moments. But where it largely failed was the conclusion. The ending was just not satisfying for most of the characters. For some of the characters predictable for others unrealistic. Overall an ok show with a bad ending.

First off, this is a very VERY adult themed show. I don't mean adult as in prophanities or r rated content, well.. that too. But the whole premise of the show and what it's trying to achieve, the theme of it and generally it's whole foundation is aimed towards a very mature audience, mature as in adult. It's not something your typical teenage daugther or son would appreciate and bing, there's a lot of situations and uncomfortable moments adults can relate to and find themself invested in, there's subtle hints and other hidden meanings that pops up through the series that if you blink you'll miss it. It's so much more than just the drama at hand or the issue that shows at that very moment in that episode, it feels like everything has a bigger meaning to it and you are watching, trying to desipher what it all means. Like that one simple conversation or that item on the table that was being focused on, you start analyzing it knowing it has a meaning or symbolizes something.  As the title says, it took me a few episodes to really get into it all and really enjoy the series. But give it a chance and hang on, it is all worth it once you get a feel for how the show is supposed to be and the way it's intended for you to enjoy. It just takes time, trust me. It's worth it.

After watching Season 1 I didn't understand why the show was so highly rated. I enjoyed it somewhat but wouldn't have thought it was worthy of so many nominations and awards. I really enjoyed the multiple storylines in the second season, especially Valentina, Mia and Lucia. At first they seemed somewhat insignificant but their characters really developed and had endearing qualities. Tom Hollander was cast perfectly in the role of Quentin. Was sceptical about the story first, but enjoyed every moment of this show. Excellent casting, complex charismatic characters and storylines, poetic settings, great dialogs and pace. And the soundtrack complements it perfectly. Watch it!

A star is born! Aimee Lou Wood brings so much fun to this season's White Lotus.  Her bunny teeth are what makes you want to know more about her. As always Mike White is the master of suspense and comedy. Every season is different and connected in some way to the previous seasons. You can guess where you think this season is going and you will be wrong again. Enjoy the journey as it's only 8 episodes and it will leave you wanting for more. Sam Rockwell is amazing and his convo with Walton Goggins is hysterical. It reminds me of the scene in Pulp Fiction where Christopher Walken delivers a watch to a young child who grows up to be Bruce Willis. He carried it, as a prisoner of war in Vietnam, along with the boy's father and promised to deliver it to his son back home.  It's so cringe and even more funny. Sam Rockwell probably just won an Emmy for this performance. Excellent!!

Loved it, all two season- binge watched them in 4 days. What I loved about it? Let's see... is how real the characters were, how real their problems , no matter how shallow or deep. Nothing is obvious, you can see good and bad, moral and immoral, excellence and vulgarity in every character. Nothing's certain, there are actions and their consequences. The details, small things that we are all confronted with each day are all into play here. And the cast- excellent - F. Murray Abraham and Michael Imperioli, just to name a couple. Also, the scenery is superb! Bravo! I hope they will make a season 3.

I had heard some positive things about this limited series so I found seasons one and two on DVD at my public library. In a nutshell, dark comedy episodes involving the super wealthy on vacation. Each season starts with a tragic incident at the end of the week of vacation, then the series is told as a flashback.  Season one, Hawaii: I became concerned early when one character, a husband, exposed his genitals to his wife as he worried that he may have cancer. In an interview Zahn, playing the character, said "I didn't even have to do that part, it's somebody else wearing a prosthetic. That's about as absurd as it gets, right?"  About that time I considered abandoning it because I wondered if the whole thing would be a series of distasteful sex and toilet humor. Fortunately I didn't and the remainder was just well-written, dark humor.  The show is a somewhat exaggerated view of what the very wealthy are like and how entitled they are in satiations such as this, a vacation at a luxury resort. And, how the resort staff resent the poor treatment.  So yes, I was entertained by the whole thing. The last episode is really dark humor and a key character dies.  Season Two, Sicily: The Jennifer Coolidge and Jon Gries characters became husband and wife after the Hawaii week, they are the only two carryovers from season one. It gradually becomes clear during the week in Italy that he is not representing himself in a totally faithful manner. She brings along her assistant (Haley Lu Richardson) to the great disapproval of her husband. It might muck up his plans.  Aside from that, we see two couples, all 35-ish. The men were roommates in college and both became very financially successful but still battled certain personality flaws. This springs some inter-couple tension.  Then there are the three men, grandfather, father, and son, whose ancestry is Scillian and they want to see if they can find distant relatives. Plus the two young hookers who like to hang around hotels to see if they can get some funding from wealthy vacationing Americans. And usually succeed.  For me the test of a series like this is if at the end of an episode, I look forward to what will happen next, and this does that for me. Highly entertaining.  The closing song over the credits is "The best things in life are free."

Jennifer Coolidge is a real delight. Without her and her character's storyline this show would be nothing. Yes, it is dark, funny, twisted, and the writing is creative and imaginative. But ultimately, watching a bunch of miserable rich people despairing over the emptiness of their lives, depressed me more than it entertained me. More importantly, it felt like something I have watched a million times before. I watched this show with some significant delay after it was hyped the way that it was. I was really disappointed as I had expected something fresh and innovative. Season 1 was okay, season 2 was just a repetition of the same stuff, brought nothing new to the table. And I have no idea how they are going to make season 3 work without Jennifer Coolidge. Honestly, without her I'm not even interested in the show.

This is one of the zaniest, most brilliant, original programmes ever made to date.  Once you realise that every character is a dysfunctional human being the whole thing clicks into place. It's huge fun and hugely funny, whilst at the same time throwing a spotlight onto the darkest recesses of human existence.  The cinematography is superb, not only because of the beautiful on-location filming, but because it's shot so darned cleverly.  The acting is across-the-board outstanding. Just brilliant characters, beautifully portrayed.  The music is as mad and wonderful and totally complementary.  When I look back in years to come and think of which programmes stood out, this will be in my top ten. It's outstanding.

The writing, acting, and level of intrigue was enough, but the biting social commentary was perfection.  Season 2 was never supposed to exist. Season 1 does unexpectedly well and a sequel is cobbled together as a money grab? It's not a movie sequel but it's the same thing.  I like Jennifer Coolidge but not here. The rest of the cast does nothing, but Theo James is truly unwatchable. Simona Tabasco is probably the best part of this season, certainly the most interesting.

Seriously after watching 2 episodes I was hooked.  Disclaimer. This is not a murder mystery type show. This is not a show about characters getting to a resort and discovering some dark secret. It is very much a show that is character focused and relies SOLELY on that. Go in expecting to see rich people living their lives at the white lotus and learning the characters and AMAZING actors who play them.  You just can't say enough good things about the actors, the humor is brilliantly dark and funny almost constantly and the drama and heart can be felt very strong at certain moments.  I'm not sure how I feel about the ending but I do know this, this is an HBO classic. It's a live or hate show and it's one of a kind. I'm not sure which genre I can even put it in.  I highly recommend just sitting down with an open mind and if the characters interest you just go for it!

I found every season to be super interesting and entertaining to watch. It's probably the only season endings where I am saying "no, no, no" and can still smile at human nature.  I actually thought season 3 was even better than the first two seasons. Some of the characters were a bit more complex than in the previous seasons and their internal battles felt more relatable - and the cast were exceptionally good at playing out their characters in a multi dimensional way that made it impossible to dislike them. In mythology lotus eaters are people who drugged themselves by eating lotus flowers, which rendered them incapable of doing anything but indulging in pleasure and luxury. In this world who are those people? The idle rich, of course.  The characters are well-drawn and acted. The use of music is excellent. The writing and direction are great. It'll probably be too subtle for many people, especially those who need to be spoon-fed everything the makers are trying to get across, but everyone else will appreciate its subtlety.  Normally when I love something I binge-watch it, but with this I had to limit myself to one episode a week. There's only six episodes, and I just had to draw the experience out it's so good.

So based on the negative reviews, it seems like if you don't have a sense of humor or are easily offended then don't watch.  However, if you like to laugh, and you like the few shows that still dare to go to dark satirical places then you are in for a very fun ride.  I can't get enough of this show. I watched it on my own, then again with family, and again with friends. I can't even remember the last time I've watched a series more than once, and each time still felt new and fun and I continued to get entertained all 3 times.  Connie Britton's character is my absolute favorite, followed by the feud between Mr Patton and Armond.  The scenery is gorgeous, the opening theme music with that wildlife wall paper is like a hypotonic way to take the viewer out of their head and into the the world of The White Lotus resort.  The storytelling and script is very strong. It's satire, it pokes fun at privilege and societal stereotypes in an over-the-top yet brilliant way. Enjoy the ride, it's a breath of fresh air.

You know where you are as soon as you hear it. Congratulations for a superb second series.  Loving Jennifer Coolidge and Will Sharpe.  It's cringey, inviting, clever and classy. I hope they get more awards and they go on to make a third series.  Well done to all the cast and crew. *****

Great story, characters, and yes, off the wall. There's not much about this show that isn't hugely overdone and strange, and that's part of its greatness. Some excellent camera work, and a musical backdrop that's used to help build the tone of specific scenes, and each episode. The show undoubtedly will hold the attention of viewers who have a dark sense of humor, and for those who don't, it will give you some perspective. The characters are complex, yet created with a sense of familiarity. As nutty as some of them are, they are on some level, very relatable. For anyone looking for a wild ride of a show, then be encouraged to stop and smell the White Lotus.

The White Lotus may, at first glance, appear like yet another tale about the wealthy and privileged, but while IT IS that, it's so much more. Following various guests at the titular luxury Hawaiian resort, the White Lotus explores themes of class, race, gender (all the buzzwords), but in a way that feels refreshing, is funny, and most of all, deeply human.  I love how there are no caricatures in this show. Even characters we'd assume to be detestable are given moments reflective of their humanity and act in ways that I think most of us could at least understand.  More than that, the script is smart enough not to pigeonhole people into archetypes or boxes. That goes for the narrative as well, which takes unexpected yet predictable-in-hindsight turns that keeps the whole thing feeling fresh.  The performances are wonderful throughout, with Jennifer Coolidge and Steve Zahn being the real standouts for me.  It's 6 episodes, it's very funny, thoughtful, beautifully shot, set on a gorgeous Hawaiian resort, and has the stunning Alexandra Daddario in one of her best roles yet. What's not to love?

The White Lotus Season 1, is a masterpiece that blends biting social satire with sun-soaked drama, cementing creator Mike White as a storytelling genius. Set at the luxurious White Lotus resort in Hawaii, the series follows a group of privileged vacationers whose idyllic getaway unravels into a web of entitlement, dysfunction, and dark comedy.  With a stellar ensemble cast and a knack for exposing human flaws, this show is an addictive, thought-provoking gem that lingers long after the credits roll.  The series hooks you from the start with a flash-forward: someone's dead, but who? From there, White masterfully peels back the layers of each character, revealing their insecurities and hypocrisies against the backdrop of a tropical paradise.  Jennifer Coolidge is a revelation as Tanya, a grieving heiress whose chaotic energy steals every scene- her performance is a highlight. She's both hilarious and heart breaking. Murray Bartlett, as the unraveling resort manager Armond, delivers a fantastic performance, a perfect mix of camp and tragedy. The rest of the cast bring depth to what could have been mere caricatures, making their flaws painfully relatable.  What sets The White Lotus apart is its razor-sharp commentary on privilege, class, and colonialism. The writing is tight, balancing humour with tension. Visually, it's a feast - opulent Hawaiian landscapes contrast with the characters' inner ugliness.  The White Lotus is a master-class in storytelling through tension and character.  A near-perfect blend of satire, drama, and dark humour, elevated by a phenomenal cast and stunning visuals. It's a beautiful escape that exposes the messiness of humanity.

I do think that season 2 is stronger than season 1 though.  Season 1 was kind of frustrating, I think I'd give that closer to a 5/10.
